lineage_context.teaching_goal: Use the local Linum flower-and-fruit plan—5 free petals, 5 stamens, 5 styles and a many-part capsule—as the family door, then contrast Malpighiaceae's clawed petals/oil-gland architecture.

project_scope.note: All five project-pool taxa are Linum. This lesson is intentionally built around the local genus rather than pretending one narrow key covers all global Linaceae.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: On a small herb, inspect one flower: usually 5 free sepals, 5 free petals, 5 stamens and 5 styles. Then confirm a superior 5-carpellate ovary that matures into a many-valved capsule.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Local Linum are annual or perennial herbs with simple narrow leaves that may be alternate, opposite or whorled low on the stem; stipules are absent or gland-like.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers are usually radial and 5-merous. Petals are free and often showy; stamens commonly 5. The ovary is superior, usually 5-carpellate, with styles commonly 5 and free or partly joined.
family_diagnostics.fruit: A dry capsule derived from a 5-carpellate ovary, often appearing 10-segmented/10-valved as false septa divide the primary locules.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: For the project pool: five free petals + five stamens + five styles + a many-part capsule is the fastest Linum package.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: 5-merous flower → five styles → capsule segmentation → Linum species doors → Malpighiales comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Flax is easiest when you stop using flower color and count the reproductive parts. The repeated five-part pattern carries straight into the capsule.

steps.title: 1 · Count the free petals
steps.look_for: Five free petals around five sepals; color may be yellow, blue or other tones depending on species.
steps.why_it_matters: Keeps the lesson structural instead of color-based.

steps.title: 2 · Find five stamens and five styles
steps.look_for: Five fertile stamens and a central ovary topped by five styles/stigmatic branches.
steps.why_it_matters: This is a stronger local flax confirmation than narrow leaves alone.

steps.title: 3 · Follow the ovary into the capsule
steps.look_for: A superior 5-carpellate ovary developing into a dry capsule that appears subdivided into multiple segments/valves.
steps.why_it_matters: Fruit architecture confirms the flower pattern after petals are gone.

steps.title: 4 · Use sepal and capsule details for species work
steps.look_for: Once family/genus is secure, compare sepal shape/margins, habit and capsule proportions rather than relying on flower color.
steps.why_it_matters: The five project flax taxa are close enough that family recognition must hand off cleanly to species morphology.

comparisons.title: Linaceae vs Malpighiaceae
comparisons.rule: Both are Malpighiales with 5-part flowers, but local Linum is radial with ordinary free petals and five styles; Malpighiaceae commonly has opposite leaves, conspicuously clawed petals, often 10 stamens and sepal oil glands.

comparisons.title: Linaceae vs Geraniaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can be 5-merous herbs. Geraniaceae commonly forms a beaked schizocarp; local Linum forms a dry many-part capsule without the geranium beak.

visual_lesson.caveat: Global Linaceae is broader than Linum. This learner deliberately keys the project's one-genus pool.

genera.fast_cue: 5 free petals + 5 stamens + 5 styles + many-part capsule
